A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the capping of the C-terminal residue in cavitand-bound peptides is not necessary for helicity and stability.
cavitand-based proteins are a useful platform for the investigation of protein folding, as the caviteins are highly helical, and their folding is well defined.
cavitands are useful scaffolds for the construction of de novo peptides, and that the caviteins have the potential to be developed into useful biologically active molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal capping efficiency of amino acids is not as well studied as the C-terminal caps.
the N-terminus of a protein is more important for stability and structure than the C-terminus.
glycine is an effective N-terminal cap, and that it is a useful residue to include in de novo peptides.
